intro: Finder for photographers on Mac is the file manager already built into macOS, and it covers most of the file work in a shoot. You batch rename frames, tag picks, convert HEIC files with Quick Actions and sort by tag without installing anything. Lazur adds voice help on top, so you can ask where a command is while you work.

blocks.text: Most photo work on a Mac starts in Finder. The card lands in a folder, the frames need names, and the picks need a way to stand out. Finder handles all three without another app. Lazur does not replace that work. It sits beside it, so you can ask out loud when you forget where a command lives.
What Finder covers for a photo shoot

Finder handles the file side of a shoot. It shows folders, previews, tags and the Trash. It also runs Quick Actions, which are small tools attached to a file. Apple's Quick Actions page lists Rotate, Markup, Trim, Create PDF, Convert Image and Remove Background. You reach them with Control-click > Quick Actions, through More, or from the Preview pane.

Finder does not edit pixels. You still need your editing app for that, whether it is Lightroom, Capture One or Photoshop. What Finder gives you is the folder structure, the names and the first sort. Get those right, and every later step gets easier.
Batch rename photos in Finder on Mac

Batch renaming is the first job most photographers need. Select the files, Control-click one of them, and choose Rename. Then pick Format. Format lets you set a name format, place an index, counter or date before or after the name, and set a starting number. Apple's rename guide describes these options.

items: Copy the card to a second drive before you touch anything.
Select the frames from one shoot. Use ⌘A for the whole folder, or Shift-click for a range.
Control-click the selection, choose Rename, then pick Format.
Type the shoot name, add a counter, and set the starting number.
Read the first and last names in the list before you confirm.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. You have a wedding folder with RAW files and JPEGs from one day. Name the shoot first, then add a counter. Give both file types the same name pattern, so each RAW lines up with its JPEG by name. A matching sequence makes pairs easy to find later.

Date formats need care. A date before the counter keeps names in day order when you sort by name. Two shoots on the same day need a shoot name too. Without it, the counters from both sets collide, and you have to rename again.

blocks.title: Renaming changes the real files
blocks.text: Batch rename changes the names on disk, not a copy of them. Keep the original card until you have checked the result. If a batch goes wrong, restore from a backup rather than guessing.
Tag picks, rejects and deliveries in Finder

Tags turn a folder into a set of filters. You can add a tag by selecting a file and using the File menu or Control-click. You can also click a color above Tags, or use the Tag button in a Finder window's toolbar. Apple's tag guide covers all three routes.

blocks.title: Keep the color set small
blocks.text: Use one color for picks, one for retouched and one for delivered. A color that means two things stops being useful. Rename or recolor tags in Finder > Settings > Tags when the set changes.

Favorite tags make the Control-click menu faster. Apple says up to seven tags can appear in that menu. To set them, drag a tag over one in the Favorite Tags section. Control-1 through Control-7 add or remove favorite tags from the keyboard. Set them once, then tag picks from the menu.
Sort photos by tag in Finder
Sorting by tag brings the picks together. Apple's tag guide gives three routes to it.

items: Menu bar: View > Show View Options > Sort By > Tags.
List view: Control-click a column header, then choose Tags.
Toolbar: click the Group button, then choose Tags.

blocks.text: Grouping suits review. Sorting suits a long list. Pick the one that matches the task in front of you.

Tag mistakes show up later. The most common one is tagging a copy and expecting the original to change. A copy in another folder is a separate file to Finder, so tags on one do not reach the other. Check the file you will deliver, not the one you used to browse.

For the exact steps, read [How to add a tag to a file in Finder on Mac](/how-to/add-a-tag-to-a-file-in-finder). For a visual pass before you tag, [gallery view](/how-to/use-gallery-view-in-finder) makes frames easier to scan.

blocks.text: Convert HEIC to JPEG in Finder with Quick Actions

Phones and some cameras save HEIC files. Some clients and web forms want JPEG. Finder's Convert Image Quick Action changes the format or the size. Apple gives HEIC to JPEG or PNG as its example. Select the files, Control-click, then open Quick Actions to find Convert Image.

Test one file before a big batch. An Apple Community thread reports that Convert Image did nothing on macOS 14.1, with no error message. A reply says it worked after an update to 14.4. Another reply says it still failed on 14.5 until Finder was relaunched. Apple's pages I checked do not confirm that relaunch fix, so treat it as a lead.

Keep the originals. A converted file is a new file, so the HEIC stays where it was. Convert a copy, open the result in Preview, and check the size and the look. Delete nothing until the client has the right set. [How to use the preview pane in Finder on Mac](/how-to/use-the-preview-pane-in-finder) covers the side panel.

Shortcuts can add your own steps to the Quick Actions menu. Apple says you can add Shortcuts from the Shortcuts app. Automator workflows can also run as extensions, reached from Finder, the Touch Bar or the Services menu. Third-party quick actions come from the Mac App Store.

items: Convert Image: HEIC to JPEG or PNG for a client who needs a standard format.
Rotate: fix a sideways phone frame before it goes into the folder.
Create PDF: one file for a proof or a contract scan.
Remove Background: a cutout for a test layout, not a final image.
Markup: notes on a file before you send it to a client.

blocks.text: Known rough spots in Finder on macOS Tahoe 26

Apple's Tahoe 26 update notes name no Finder change. Other writers have found changes that matter for photo folders. Daring Fireball, in January 2026, reports a View Option that resizes all columns to fit the longest visible filename. The author says it was a hidden preference for a few years and calls it an early prototype.

Auto-resize only measures names you can see right now. A long name further down the list does not change the width until it scrolls into view. For mixed names, switch to List view, turn on the resize option, then scroll the folder once to check the fit.

The same report describes a layering bug. Rename an item that is scrolled under the sidebar, and Tahoe draws the rename field on top of the sidebar. On macOS 15 Sequoia, the column snaps next to the sidebar. Scroll the item fully into view before you rename it. That is a workaround to try, not a confirmed fix.
Back up photos before you sort in Finder

Sorting is where mistakes hurt most. A bad batch rename, an accidental delete or a drag into the wrong folder can cost you a shoot. Backblaze's 2022 survey asked US adults about data loss. It was not a photographer survey, but the numbers show how common the problem is.

The survey found 54% of computer owners had lost data. It found 67% had accidentally deleted something. The margin of error was ±2.8 points at 95% confidence, from a sample of 2,068 US adults. Treat these as general numbers, not a photographer rate.
A simple habit helps. Copy the card to one drive, then work on a second copy. Keep the first copy until the delivery is done. This is general advice, not a Finder feature, but it uses disk space.

If a file goes missing, check the Trash before you panic. Emptying the Trash removes those files for good, so do not empty it during a shoot. The steps are in [How to restore a file from the trash in Finder on Mac](/how-to/restore-a-file-from-the-trash-in-finder).
Where Lazur helps during a Finder session

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time.

A wedding card from start to finish

Here is one shoot, start to finish, using Finder and a single assistant. The card holds RAW and JPEG frames from a wedding. The client wants picks, a set of HEIC conversions and a clean delivery folder. Work through the steps in order, because each one depends on the last.

items: Copy the card to a working drive and a backup drive.
Open the working copy and switch to List view.
Select the frames you keep, Control-click, and choose a pick color.
Sort by tag with View > Show View Options > Sort By > Tags, and check the picks sit together.
Batch rename the picks with Control-click > Rename > Format.
Convert the HEIC picks with Convert Image, after a test file opens correctly.
Copy the delivery folder to a new location, then check the first and last names.

blocks.text: Order matters. Rename after the picks are tagged, not before. Renaming a file does not remove its tags, so the picks keep their color. Convert after the rename, then check the names again. Copy the final folder last, so you deliver the checked set.
Common Finder mistakes with photo folders

items: Renaming the only copy of a card. Copy first, rename second, check third.
Tagging a copy and expecting the original to change. Copies are separate files to Finder.
Using a date format alone when two shoots share a day. Add the shoot name or a counter.
Trusting Convert Image on a large batch. Convert one file, then open it in Preview.
Emptying the Trash during a job. Anything in it goes for good, so wait until delivery is done.

blocks.text: The last mistake is skipping the check. Look at the first and last names, open one converted file, and check one tag color. Those checks take a few seconds each. Skip them, and you find the problem at the client's desk.
Next steps for Finder on Mac

Start with one shoot. Set up a small set of tags, add the favorites, and run one batch rename on a copy. Then repeat the same steps on the next shoot. A routine you repeat beats a clever trick you forget. If a frame goes missing from the list, [How to search for a file in Finder on Mac](/how-to/search-for-a-file-in-finder) shows the fastest way back to it.

If you want Lazur, start the trial and try it on a real folder. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the Rename command is, or ask how to convert one file. The answer comes out loud, and Lazur circles the spot on screen. Ask it to walk you through the steps one at a time, and keep your hand on the mouse.

faq.question: Is Finder for photographers on Mac a separate app?
faq.answer: No. Finder is the file manager built into macOS, so you do not install it. Batch rename, tags and Quick Actions all use Finder's own menus. Lazur adds voice help on top, and it needs its own install and trial.

faq.question: Can Finder rename a whole photo shoot at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Select the files, Control-click, choose Rename, then pick Format. Set a name format, add a counter or date, and set a starting number. Check the first and last names before you confirm.

faq.question: Can Finder convert HEIC to JPEG?
faq.answer: Yes, with the Convert Image Quick Action, which changes the format or the size. Apple's example is HEIC to JPEG or PNG. Test one file first, because an Apple Community thread reports it did nothing on macOS 14.1.

faq.question: How many tags can I keep in the Control-click menu?
faq.answer: Apple says up to seven. Drag a tag over one in the Favorite Tags section to set it. Control-1 through Control-7 add or remove favorite tags from the keyboard.

faq.question: Does Lazur rename or edit my photos for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides and points. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. You do the clicks, and Lazur waits for each one before it moves on.

faq.question: Does Lazur see my photos all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Is there a Windows version of Lazur?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: What is the rename field bug on macOS Tahoe?
faq.answer: Daring Fireball reports that on macOS Tahoe, the rename field can draw over the sidebar when the item is scrolled under it. Sequoia snaps the column next to the sidebar. Scrolling the item into view first is a workaround to try, not a confirmed fix.

faq.question: Are the Backblaze numbers about photographers?
faq.answer: No. The 2022 Backblaze survey sampled 2,068 US adults, and 1,861 of them own a computer. It found 54% of computer owners had lost data. The margin of error is ±2.8 points at 95% confidence.
